advice: Experiment: in each generated 512-step compute loop, test a four-accumulator software pipeline that separates operand loads from FMOPA by one K iteration. Keep four ZA tiles and one FMOPA group per K step. Add a one-step prologue and drain; load the next A/B vectors into spare registers, compute with the current vectors, then rotate register roles. This differs from the tried unroll variants and the prior preload proposal by using an explicit load/compute pipeline. Hypothesis: it may overlap operand-load latency with FMOPA work. This is unverified advice, not a measured fact.
risks: The register assignments and pointer advances need careful review: each loop must process exactly K=0..511 in order, with no out-of-range load or skipped/duplicated contribution. Check assembler legality and live-register use. Keep the ABI, streaming transitions, fallback, packing behavior, and full BSD notice unchanged. Validate the fixed benchmark and general-size odd/tail and n<=0 cases at tolerance .002. Measure with fresh paired controls on the same power source and settings; report spread and do not infer a gain from noisy scores.
